newsitem.title: CHILE: Chilean shares add another day to bull run.
newsitem.headline: Chilean shares add another day to bull run.

text.p: Chilean blue chips closed two- and-a-half points higher as strong foreign demand and expectations of a Central Bank rate cut combined to push the bolsa into the second, rousing day of a New Year's rally.
The blue-chip IPSA index ended 2.47 percent higher at 105.77 points, off about a point from afternoon highs.
The all-share IGPA was up 1.47 percent to 5050.39 points on moderate volume of 141 million shares traded.
Brokers attributed the rise to a heady mix of demand from foreign institutional investors looking for bargains and non-stop rumors of an early relaxing in local interest rates.
"Everyone was dumping Chile a while back and now investors are looking for value and they're finding it in Chile," said Lance Eckel, analyst at brokers Sud Americano.
He said the unspectacular volume -- 18 billion pesos -- suggested local demand was low and the real impetus was coming from New York, particularly from mutual funds.
Some brokers stressed feelings that the Central Bank was moving closer to a long-expected cut in interest rates, though the timing of any such move was far from clear.
Central Bank sources said they knew of no such move imminently.
A mild improvement in copper prices and strong gains on other Latin American bourses and the Dow all contributed to the bullish mood, said brokers.
"People sold too much in December. They put all their losses in the 1996 side and now everything looks cheap," said a broker at a major Santiago brokerage.

Market-watchers disagreed on how long the rally could last. Brokers spoke of a "change in the mood" on the bourse, but Eckel pointed out the rise was still a long way from erasing 1996's losses and could be seen as essentially technical.
Shares in nearly every major sector rose, including forestry and telecommuncations. Among electricals, Endesa was up 3.3 percent to 226.5 pesos and Enersis rose 2.6 percent to 237 pesos.
Compaa de Telecomunicaciones de Chile A series was up 3.2 percent to 2570 pesos and supermarket chain Santa Isabel rose 3.9 percent to 660 pesos.
